Synopsis:
    Treasury yields are rising sharply (10-year at 4.79%, up 80bps since March), approaching the psychologically critical 5% level. While S&P 500 has held up (+11% YTD) supported by strong earnings, analysts warn that with Q2 earnings season in the rearview, markets will now be more exposed to macro headwinds. Key risks: sticky inflation, fiscal deficit expansion, and a hawkish turn from new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. AI-driven equity valuations carry embedded duration risk, making them particularly vulnerable to further yield spikes. S&P 500 forward P/E at 19.7 remains above long-term average of 16.
